sentences.text:
While placing on record, copy of letter dated 6.9.2023 issued under the signatures of Deputy
Commissioner, Shimla, learned Additional Advocate General sates that instructions have been
issued to Superintendent of Police to ensure that obstruction, if any, on the road in question is
removed forthwith.

2.  At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioners sates that pursuant to order dated 4.9.2023,
obstruction caused on the road in question stands removed.
3.

Learned counsel for respondent No.6 and 7 states that under the garb of order dated 4.9.2023,
efforts are being made to encroach upon private land of the respondents Nos. 6 and 7, and after passing of order, unauthorized construction is being raised on private land, which fact has been seriously disputed by learned counsel for the petitioners.

4. Having taken note of allegations leveled in the petition, that link road starting .
from Harizan Basti Jharangta to HB Shakti Nagar 0/0 to 4/0 kms is being obstructed, this court passed order dated 4.9.2023, specifically directing Deputy Commissioner Shimla to ensure that obstruction, if any, on the road starting from Harizan Basti Jharangta to HB Shakti Nagar be removed.
Pursuant to aforesaid of direction, obstruction caused on the spot has been removed, as has been fairly acknowledged by the learned counsel for the petitioners.

5. During proceedings, it is transpired that respondents Nos. 6 and 7 have filed rt some civil suit in the competent court of law, for restraining the Public Works Department from using private land of respondents Nos. 6 and 7 for construction of road, if any, without acquiring the land in terms of provisions of Land Acquisition Act 6.

Though, Mr. Kulbhushan Khajuria, Advocate for respondents Nos. 6 and 7 vehemently argued that under the garb of order dated 4.9.2023, private land of the petitioners comprised in Khasra No.
153, 155, 156 and 674/563 in village Mandharli is being used /encroached by Public Works Department, but bare perusal of order dated 4.9.2023, clearly reveals that the respondent Department was directed to remove obstruction, if any, from Harizan Basti Jharangta to HB Shakti Nagar road, which is beyond aforesaid village of petitioner, as is evident from map placed on record as Annexure P-3.
7.

Respondents Nos.6 and 7 in their reply have stated that the land belonging to them, if required,
can be used by the Department for construction of road, in accordance with law, meaning thereby private respondents though have no opposition to use of land for road, but they want proper compensation for that as such, Department may take appropriate decision so that dispute is settled for all times to come.

. 
8. Mr. Kulbhushan Khajuria, Advocate, for respondents Nos. 6 and 7 states that no undue obstruction shall be caused by his clients in free movement of public as well as vehicles.

2 9.

Since it is not in dispute, rather evident from record that the road detailed of herein above, came to be constructed out of public funds, public of area concerned has right to use the same without there being obstruction and as such, this court deems it fit to dispose of the present petition with a direction to respondents to rt ensure that the road from Harizan Basti Jharangta to Shakti Nagar, is not obstructed by anybody.
Dispute, if any, with regard to ownership, as is sought to be raised by respondents Nos. 6 and 7 shall be decided by civil court, for which respondents Nos. 6 and 7 have already filed civil suit.

It is also clarified that no damage shall be caused to private property of respondents Nos. 6 and 7 excluding the road, while implementing direction contained in order dated 4.9.2023, which is made absolute.
10. Petition stands disposed of in the afore terms, alongwith all pending applications.

(Sandeep Sharma) Judge September 12, 2023 (Vikrant)
